title: Undefined control sequence
explanation: You used a command that LaTeX does not know — usually a typo, or a package that provides it was not loaded.
fix: Check the spelling of the command. If it comes from a package, add the matching \usepackage{...} to your preamble.

title: Missing $ inserted
explanation: LaTeX found a math-only symbol (like _ or ^ or a Greek letter) outside of math mode.
fix: Wrap the math parts in $...$ (or \(...\)), or escape a literal underscore with \_.

title: Missing $ right
explanation: LaTeX reached the end of a paragraph while still inside math mode opened with $.
fix: Close the math with a matching $ on the same paragraph.

title: Display math should end with $$
explanation: A $$...$$ block was not closed properly.
fix: Make sure every $$ has a matching closing $$.

title: File not found
explanation: A file (package, class or image) could not be found.
fix: Check the file name and path. If it is a package, install it with your TeX distribution’s package manager.

title: Missing \begin{document}
explanation: LaTeX found text before \begin{document}, or the document environment is missing.
fix: Add \begin{document} after the preamble (everything after \documentclass).

title: Extra alignment tab has been changed to \cr
explanation: A table row has more & separators than columns defined in the tabular preamble.
fix: Remove the extra & or add a column (l/c/r) to the tabular definition.

title: Misplaced alignment tab &
explanation: An & was used outside of a tabular or alignment environment.
fix: Escape a literal ampersand as \&, or move it into a tabular/align environment.

title: Too many }’s
explanation: There is an unmatched closing brace }.
fix: Remove the extra }, or add the matching opening brace {.

title: Runaway argument
explanation: A command argument was not closed before the end of the file or paragraph — usually a missing }.
fix: Look at the command in the error line and close its braces.

title: Paragraph ended before command was complete
explanation: A command that must keep its argument in one paragraph hit a blank line.
fix: Remove the blank line inside the command’s argument, or wrap the argument in braces.

title: Reference undefined
explanation: A \ref points to a label that does not exist (or a second compile run is needed).
fix: Check the label name for typos; run the compile again — LaTeX needs two passes for cross-references.

title: Citation undefined
explanation: A \cite key is not present in the bibliography, or BibTeX/Biber has not run yet.
fix: Check the key in your .bib file and compile again (latexmk handles the bibliography passes).

title: Environment undefined
explanation: The \begin{...} environment is not defined — often a missing package (e.g. align needs amsmath).
fix: Load the package that provides the environment, e.g. \usepackage{amsmath} for align.

title: Bibliography file problem
explanation: BibTeX could not find a \bibliography command or the .aux file is broken.
fix: Make sure \bibliography{...} or \addbibresource{...} is present, and delete stale files in .verso/build, then recompile.

title: Biber error
explanation: Biber (the biblatex backend) reported an error or is not installed.
fix: Read the Biber message above; if it is missing, install biber via your TeX distribution.

pattern: Font \\[^=]+=[^ ]+ at|Font shape .* undefined|The font .* cannot be found
title: Font problem
explanation: The requested font is not installed or the name is wrong (common with XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX and fontspec).
fix: Check the font name with fc-list, install the font, or use a font that ships with TeX Live.

title: Overfull box
explanation: A line (or box) is too wide and sticks into the margin — a warning, not an error.
fix: Rephrase the sentence, allow a hyphenation point (\-), or add \sloppy.

title: Underfull box
explanation: A line is too loosely spaced — usually caused by forced line breaks or \\ in text.
fix: Usually harmless. Rewrite the sentence or remove the manual line break.

pattern: no line here to end|There.s no line here to end
title: No line here to end
explanation: A \\ line break appears where no line exists (e.g. directly after \begin{...}).
fix: Remove the \\ or add content before it.

title: Too many unprocessed floats
explanation: Too many figures/tables were queued without being placed.
fix: Add \clearpage at a suitable spot, or place floats closer to their text.

title: Option clash for package
explanation: The same package was loaded twice with different options.
fix: Search your preamble (and loaded packages) for duplicated \usepackage lines and merge the options.

title: Command already defined
explanation: A \newcommand redefines an existing command.
fix: Use \renewcommand instead, or rename your command.

pattern: Invalid UTF-8 byte|Unicode character .* not set up
title: Encoding problem
explanation: The file contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8, or a Unicode character has no LaTeX mapping.
fix: Save the file as UTF-8 (Verso does this by default). For exotic symbols, use \DeclareUnicodeCharacter or the symbol’s macro.

pattern: Cannot determine size of graphic|not a PDF|Graphic .* not found|could not be imported
title: Graphics problem
explanation: An included graphic is missing, in the wrong format, or corrupted.
fix: Check the file name in \includegraphics and the file type (pdflatex supports .png/.jpg/.pdf).

title: File permission problem
explanation: LaTeX could not write a file — the folder may be read-only or the file locked by a viewer.
fix: Close viewers that have the PDF open and check the folder’s write permissions.

title: Emergency stop
explanation: LaTeX aborted because of an earlier error, often a missing file or an interrupted prompt.
fix: Fix the first error in the list, then recompile.

title: Missing structure inserted
explanation: A math or alignment structure is incomplete (missing \right, \cr or \end).
fix: Complete the structure: close \left...\right pairs and environment bodies.

title: Package not found
explanation: A package is not installed in your TeX distribution.
fix: Install it with your TeX distribution’s package manager (see the command below).

title: Duplicate PDF destination
explanation: hyperref found two identical labels/names (e.g. two figures with the same caption id).
fix: Make the labels unique — often a repeated \label or duplicate section number.
